- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in the last 1–2 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon prices, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After a price spike (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 10+ days, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30d forecasts, if model’s first 5–7 days are above true outcome, reduce subsequent days by 0.5–1.0% per day to correct for overconfidence.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat, model tends to overreact; suppress upward momentum in forecast unless confirmed by technical indicators.
